top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) rests on a distinct, reproduced step: the magic wavelength cancels the trap-induced shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated together, a capability not covered by the 1997, 2005 or 2012 prizes. It has the cleanest two-name allocation on the slate and the broadest committee support. Residual risks are overlap, priority history unchecked against primary papers, and compressed credit for the Paris and NIST groups. P002 ranks second because its credit chain is incomplete without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and P000 is last because both proposals are mature and defensible.
recusal_note: No documented collaboration with Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp; long-time collaboration with 2023 laureate Anne L'Huillier and membership of the broader atomic, molecular and optical community could bias judgement of P001, but no recusal is requested.
